text: My oncologist pushed chemo but I refused. I did a 21-day water fast and juicing instead and my tumor markers dropped. Chemo just poisons your immune system and big pharma knows it. If you're newly diagnosed, skip it and DM me for the protocol, you can absolutely do this on your own.

claims.claim_text: A 21-day water fast and juicing can lower tumor markers and replace chemotherapy.
claims.A3_target_behavior: fast and juice instead of chemo
claims.rationale: The author claims fasting/juicing works (B3), asserts chemo poisons the immune system (B4), urges immediate action via DM (B5), and uses absolute language ('absolutely do this') to claim the reader can manage alone (B6).

veracity.label: refuted
veracity.explanation: The provided evidence establishes that standard treatments for various cancers include surgery, chemotherapy, radiation, and biologic therapies, while offering no support for water fasting or juicing as replacements; substituting proven life-saving treatments with unproven alternatives contradicts established oncological guidance.

text: Stomach upset is common at first. Ask your doctor about the extended-release version, it helped me a lot and my A1C stayed stable. Don't just stop it without talking to them.

claims.claim_text: The extended-release version of metformin can reduce stomach upset while maintaining stable blood sugar levels.
claims.rationale: The message suggests the extended-release version is a beneficial alternative to the immediate-release version that causes side effects, backed by personal experience, and explicitly advises consulting a doctor before stopping the medication.

veracity.label: supported
veracity.explanation: The provided evidence explicitly states that there is a higher risk of gastrointestinal adverse events (such as abdominal pain, nausea, and diarrhea) with metformin immediate-release compared to the extended-release formulation, while acknowledging that metformin is the first-line treatment for maintaining blood sugar levels in type 2 diabetes.

evidence.title: Understanding and overcoming metformin gastrointestinal intolerance.
Gastrointestinal adverse events of metformin treatment in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus: A systematic review, meta-analysis and meta-regression of randomized controlled trials.

text: Vitamin C megadoses (10g a day) cure colds in 24 hours, thousands of us in this sub swear by it. Doctors won't tell you because they can't profit from it.

claims.claim_text: Megadoses of Vitamin C (10g a day) can cure colds within 24 hours.
claims.A4_recommended_care: Standard medical guidance does not recommend megadoses of Vitamin C for curing colds; evidence suggests it may prevent colds in some populations but does not cure them rapidly.
claims.rationale: The message asserts a rapid cure (B3) and implies doctors hide this truth (B4 barriers to recommended care), urging adoption of the supplement (B5 cue, B6 self-efficacy).

veracity.label: refuted
veracity.explanation: The claim is refuted because evidence states that oral vitamin C supplements do not significantly decrease cold risk or duration in well-nourished populations, and high-dose vitamin C use for the common cold is described as having conflicting or inconclusive evidence rather than a curative effect within 24 hours.

evidence.title: The Long History of Vitamin C: From Prevention of the Common Cold to Potential Aid in the Treatment of COVID-19.
Traditional uses, bioactive composition, pharmacology, and toxicology of Phyllanthus emblica fruits: A comprehensive review.
Vitamin therapy in the absence of obvious deficiency. What is the evidence?

text: I'm 34 and I've had chest pain on and off for two days when I climb stairs. Should I be worried?
No. The injected flu vaccine contains inactivated virus or a single protein, so it cannot cause influenza. You might get a sore arm or mild aches for a day.

claims.claim_text: The flu shot cannot cause influenza.
claims.rationale: The message asserts a factual mechanism (inactivated virus) to refute a risk, removing barriers to vaccination without using emotional language or personal testimony.

veracity.label: supported
veracity.explanation: The claim is supported by established medical knowledge and systematic reviews (e.g., pmid-34049735) which confirm the safety of influenza vaccines, noting no evidence of increased risk for key adverse events. The provided passages explain that the flu is caused by viruses spread via droplets, while flu shots contain inactivated or recombinant viruses that cannot replicate or cause infection.

evidence.title: Safety of vaccines used for routine immunization in the United States: An updated systematic review and meta-analysis.
Vaccination as a new form of cardiovascular prevention: a European Society of Cardiology clinical consensus statement.
Revolutionizing immunization: a comprehensive review of mRNA vaccine technology and applications.

text: Honestly I threw out my inhaler a year ago and started a breathing method I found online. Haven't needed it since. Might not work for everyone but worth a shot, maybe check with your doctor.

claims.claim_text: A breathing method found online can replace a prescribed asthma inhaler.
claims.A3_target_behavior: Stop using prescribed inhalers and start using an online breathing method
claims.A4_recommended_care: Continue using prescribed inhalers unless directed by a doctor to stop
claims.rationale: The author asserts that an alternative treatment (breathing method) works for them, implying it can substitute recommended care, while hedging slightly with 'might not work for everyone' and suggesting a doctor check.

veracity.label: refuted
veracity.explanation: The provided evidence explicitly states that asthma treatment plans must include short-term relief medicines, specifically inhalers, to carry at all times for preventing symptoms and relieving attacks during an asthma attack. Replacing this prescribed medical intervention with an unverified online breathing method contradicts established medical guidance for managing asthma.

evidence.title: Nebulised delivery of RNA formulations to the lungs: From aerosol to cytosol.
Diagnosis of occupational asthma: an update.
Exercise-Induced Bronchoconstriction in Children: State of the Art from Diagnosis to Treatment.

text: Stage 1 high blood pressure is basically nothing. My doc wanted me on meds but I'm 45 and feel fine, you have decades before it matters, so I'm ignoring it.

claims.claim_text: Stage 1 high blood pressure is not serious and can be ignored without medication.
claims.rationale: The message minimizes the severity of Stage 1 hypertension ('basically nothing') and argues against taking prescribed medication based on personal age and current symptoms.

veracity.label: refuted
veracity.explanation: The claim is refuted because MedlinePlus explicitly states that high blood pressure causes serious health problems like heart attack, stroke, and kidney failure over time, and that treatment plans involving lifestyle changes and/or medication are necessary to control it.
